questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl is diagnosed with leukemia and begins chemotherapy in preparation for a bone marrow transplant. Two months later, gross hematuria develops, and the patient begins to complain of occasional incontinence. It is determined that these symptoms are caused by one of her chemotherapeutic agents. Coadministration of what medication might have prevented the patient’s condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mesna
  • The patient is experiencing hemorrhagic cystitis, a well-known complication of cyclophosphamide treatment. Cyclophosphamide produces a metabolite known as acrolein, which is toxic to the bladder epithelium and can lead to hemorrhagic cystitis. Coadministration of mesna with cyclophosphamide can prevent hemorrhagic cystitis.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man presents to a urologic oncologist with a painless, solid testicular mass. A diagnostic evaluation including scrotal ultrasound, radiographic studies, serum markers, and positron emission tomography scan is performed. The patient is diagnosed with low-risk disseminated seminoma. The physician tells the patient that the standard treatment is three cycles of a combination of etoposide, cisplatin, and a third agent that can cause pulmonary fibrosis. What is the mechanism of action of this third agent?

options.label: B
options.text: Generation of free radicals that cause single dsDNA breaks

questions.answerText: Generation of free radicals that cause single dsDNA breaks
questions.solutionHtml:
Generation of free radicals that cause single dsDNA breaks
  • Bleomycin is a part of the BEP regimen for treating testicular cancer (bleomycin, etoposide, and cisplatin). It is also used in the treatment of Hodgkin lymphoma. It is an antineoplastic antibiotic that halts cell division by generating free radicals that cause single double-stranded DNA breaks. The major adverse reactions are pulmonary fibrosis and hyperpigmentation. Although busulfan, an alkylating agent, can also cause pulmonary fibrosis, it is more commonly used for the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old female with a history of breast cancer that was successfully treated with trastuzumab 3 years prior now returns with a breast lump she palpated on self-exam. After imaging and biopsy, it is determined that the cancer has returned. You decide to begin her on trastuzumab therapy once again; however, her returning cancer is now unresponsive to this drug. Which of the following is a possible mechanism responsible for the chemotherapy resistance in this patient?

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased tumor expression of the bcl-2 proto-oncogene

options.label: C
options.text: Increased drug excretion through the kidneys

options.label: D
options.text: Tumor cell alteration of drug target

questions.answerText: Tumor cell alteration of drug target
questions.solutionHtml:
Tumor cell alteration of drug target
  • Cancer cells acquire many mutations as time progresses because of their inherent genomic instability. Similar to bacteria acquiring resistance to antibiotics, chemotherapies can kill all susceptible cells and leave only cells that have acquired mutations to chemotherapy targets, thus making the drug ineffective. This patient’s tumor has developed acquired resistance to trastuzumab, a monoclonal antibody that acts against the cell surface HER2 receptor.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who recently emigrated from Southeast Asia comes to her physician’s office with uterine enlargement, a vaginal mass, and vaginal bleeding. A biopsy of the vaginal mass yields A diagnosis of choriocarcinoma, and the patient is started on the usual therapeutic agent for this condition. After several weeks of therapy, the patient develops mild icterus; an enlarged, red, painful tongue; and sores in the corners of the mouth. Her complete blood cell count returns: WBCs: 2000/mm3 Hemoglobin: 9.0 g/dl Hematocrit: 26.4% Platelets: 90,000/mm3 Which of the following would most likely treat her abnormal cell count?

options.label: D
options.text: Administration of increased doses of the chemotherapy agent

questions.solutionHtml:
Administration of folinic acid
  • This patient has mucositis, glossitis, and myelosuppression secondary to methotrexate treatment. Methotrexate is a folate analog that acts by inhibiting the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase, which is responsible for converting folic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid.
  • Tetrahydrofolic acid is responsible for the synthesis of several amino acids, purines, and thymidine, a required molecule for DNA synthesis. By inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase, methotrexate induces a deficiency of tetrahydrofolic acid in the setting of normal folate levels.
  • Methotrexate toxicity must therefore be treated by providing reduced folate (folinic acid, also known as leucovorin) rather than folic acid, known as a “leucovorin rescue.”


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old male patient who is being treated for acute lymphoblastic T-cell lymphoma begins to experience severe flank pain, dysuria, vomiting, and altered mental status 5 days after the initiation of chemotherapy. Laboratory studies show the following, with normal values for a 10-year-old male in parentheses: Serum Na+: 144 mEq/L (135-145 mEq/L) Serum K+: 5.6 mEq/L (3.6-5.2 mEq/L) Serum Ca2+: 9.2 mEq/L (8.7-10.3 mg/dL) Serum phosphorus: 6.5 mg/dl (3.0-6.0 mg/dL) Serum uric acid: 7.9 mg/dl (2.0-5.5 mg/dL) Which of the following drugs is most appropriate as prophylaxis for this patient’s condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Allopurinol
  • Lysis of tumor cells following chemotherapy results in the release of potassium, uric acid, and phosphorus, leading to hyperkalemia, hyperuricemia, and hyperphosphatemia with secondary hypocalcemia. These metabolic abnormalities can then lead to renal failure and possibly multiple organ failure and death. This syndrome can be prevented with aggressive intravenous hydration and the administration of allopurinol.
  • Allopurinol is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that reduces uric acid production. Keep in mind that normal uric acid levels in children are lower than those for adults (2.0-5.5 mg/dL.) Uric acid production increases dramatically during puberty, and males reach adult uric acid levels between the ages of 12 and 14. Therefore, it is possible for a preadolescent child suffering from tumor lysis syndrome to have a uric acid level less than that of a normal adult.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a 40-pack-year history of smoking presents with weakness, fatigue, and cough. Laboratory studies show hypokalemic alkalosis without a history of vomiting or diarrhea. Levels of cortisol and ACTH are found to be high in both plasma and urine, which are unaffected by either administration of high-dose dexamethasone or corticotropin-releasing hormone. An MRI of the chest shows an unresectable centrally located lung mass. Which of the following is the best available medical treatment to prevent the development of centripetal obesity and moon facies in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ketoconazole
  • Ketoconazole is an antifungal agent that is used to treat systemic fungal infections by inhibiting fungal 14-a-demethylase. Furthermore, in patients with ectopic ACTH-secreting tumors (the most common of which is small cell lung cancer), ketoconazole or metyrapone can be used to inhibit ACTH effects and thus mitigate the progression to a Cushingoid appearance. Ketoconazole does this by inhibiting human 11-~-hydroxylase, which reduces adrenal production of cortisol in response to ACTH.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man presents with a large lump in his right testicle. Both serum a-fetoprotein and 13-human chorionic gonadotropin are elevated, and ultrasound of the testicle suggests a malignancy. The mass is resected and a retroperitoneal lymph node dissection is performed, which reveals significant nodal spread. The patient is started on adjuvant chemotherapy, but after several months develops dyspnea. Chest x-ray demonstrates ground-glass opacities. Which chemotherapeutic agent could have contributed to this adverse effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bleomycin
  • Bleomycin inhibits DNA synthesis by binding to DNA and causing single-strand and double-strand breaks. An adverse effect of bleomycin is pulmonary fibrosis


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man with non-Hodgkin lymphoma has been undergoing treatment with cyclophosphamide for the past 4 months. At his biweekly visit, he tells his doctor that for the past day or so, he has noticed a reddish tinge in his urine. In addition, he has a moderate amount of pain in the suprapubic region and complains of burning when he urinates. The physician suspects a potentially dangerous drug-related complication. What is the mechanism of the drug that is commonly given to combat this likely complication?
questions.solutionHtml:
Binding of toxic metabolites
  • Hemorrhagic cystitis is a serious condition that occurs in cancer patients due to radiation, chemotherapy, and infections. It is characterized by diffuse mucosal inflammation and hemorrhage of the entire bladder. Chemotherapeutic drugs can cause hemorrhagic cystitis when they are directly infused into the bladder for superficial bladder cancers or when excreted drugs contact the bladder epithelium.
  • The alkylating agent 'cyclophosphamide and ifosfamide are the chemotherapeutic agents most likely to cause hemorrhagic cystitis. The condition is a result of the renal excretion of acrolein, a hepatic metabolite of these drugs. Mesna is a sulfhydryl compound that is an effective neuroprotective agent for patients undergoing treatment with either cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old woman presents with a 1-week history of slurred speech and gait disturbances. Her medical history is significant for coronary artery disease and chronic kidney disease. She is a retired schoolteacher and has a 50-pack-year smoking history. CT of the chest reveals a 4-cm lung mass and mediastinal adenopathy. Laboratory tests show elevated anti-Hu and anti-Yo antibody levels. The patient is admitted to the hospital and started on combination therapy with a platinum agent and etoposide. What is the mechanism of action of etoposide?

options.label: B
options.text: The covalent intersternal linkage of DNA leads to DNA inactivation

options.label: C
options.text: The direct inhibition of anaphase through stabilizing polymerized microtubules

options.label: D
options.text: The inhibition of topoisomerase II, leading to increased DNA degradation

questions.answerText: The inhibition of topoisomerase II, leading to increased DNA degradation
questions.solutionHtml:
The inhibition of topoisomerase II, leading to increased DNA degradation
  • This patient is presenting with a paraneoplastic syndrome, evidenced by her neurologic symptoms and anti-Hu and anti-Yo antibodies, in association with small cell lung cancer (SCLC). These autoantibodies have been associated with an encephalomyelitis with a diverse array of presenting features that include slurred speech and gait anomalies. Her smoking history puts her at risk for SCLC.
  • Treatment for SCLC involves a platinum agent such as carboplatin or cisplatin in combination with etoposide. The stabilization of the topoisomerase II-DNA complex during the S and G2 phases of the cell cycle by etoposide results in the induction of double-stranded DNA breaks and prevents the completion of the G2 phase. Side effects of etoposide include bone marrow suppression, alopecia, and nausea and vomiting.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: A 37-year-old woman is diagnosed with stage IIA breast cancer and subsequently has a 3-cm tumor surgically removed. No lymph nodes are found to be positive during dissection. Because her tumor was estrogen receptor positive, her oncologist decides to prescribe a specific long-term oral chemotherapeutic medication to help prevent recurrence or relapse. What is a potential adverse effect of the medication most likely prescribed?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hot flashes
  • Since the patient’s tumor is ER-positive, raloxifene or tamoxifen were likely prescribed. These drugs are selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) that bind the estrogen receptor and have both agonist and antagonist activity, depending upon the tissue. Both drugs are antagonists at the breasts, which helps prevent the growth, survival, and division of ER-positive cancer cells, thereby preventing recurrenc The mechanism by which these drugs cause hot flashes is due to their antagonistic effects. Estrogen withdrawal at the level of the hypothalamus results in thermoregulatory dysfunction and subsequent temperature dysregulation.


Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page No. 1315.

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs causes hemorrhagic cystitis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cyclophosphamide

Cyclophosphamide causes hemorrhagic cystitis

  • Mesna is used to prevent it and acrolein(a metabolite of Cyclophosphamide) is responsible for hemorrhagic cystitis


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 918,919

questions.stem: The Alkylating agent used to induce diabetes in experimental animals is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Streptozocin

Streptozocin is a naturally occurring alkylating antineoplastic agent that is particularly toxic to the insulin-producing beta cells of the pancreas in mammals. It is ubeforeedicine for treating certain cancers of the islets of Langerhans and used in medical research to produce an animal model for hyperglycemia and Alzheimer's in a large dose.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 305

questions.stem: Among the following options, the most neurotoxic alkylating agent is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ifosfamide

Ifosfamide:

  • is the most neurotoxic of the alkylating agents
  • It may produce altered mental status, coma, generalized seizures, and cerebellar ataxia
  • Ifosfamide produces greater neurotoxicity (mental changes, hallucinations, seizures, coma) and hemorrhagic cystitis than other alkylating agents.
  • To protect the bladder, MESNA, a –SH compound is mostly given with it. Mesna is excreted in urine—binds and inactivates the radiotoxic metabolites of ifosfamide and cyclophosphamide.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 919

questions.stem: Which of the following drug can cause flagellate hyperpigmentation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Bleomycin

Bleomycin causes flagellate hyperpigmentation

  • there will be bands of pruritic erythema on the arms, back, scalp, and hands
  • This rash responds readily to topical corticosteroids


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 927

questions.stem: Among the following options, Ifosfamide is a :
questions.solutionHtml:
Alkylating agents

Alkylating agents any highly reactive drug that binds to certain chemical groups (phosphate, amino, sulfhydryl, hydroxyl, and imidazole groups) commonly found in nucleic acids and other macromolecules, bringing about changes in the DNA and RNA of cells.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 919

questions.stem: Which of the following drugs causes persistent leucopenia?
questions.solutionHtml:
Carmustine

Carmustines used to treat cancer of the lymphatic system, brain, and certain types of cancers of bone marrow. It may also be used to treat other types of cancer. It can be used alone, or together with certain other medicines as part of combination chemotherapy.



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Chapter 66, Page No. 1174, 1175.

questions.stem: Alkalinization of urine ameliorates the toxicity of which of the following drugs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Methotrexate
  • Alkalinization of urine speeds the clearance of weakly acidic drugs e.g. aspirin, Phenobarbital, chlorpropamide, and Methotrexate, etc.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 989

questions.stem: A patient with Wilms’ tumor is receiving a chemotherapeutic agent that is described as working by intercalating into DNA strands, and that is efficacious regardless of which stage of the cell cycle the tumor cells are in. Which of the following agents best fits this description?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dactinomycin (actinomycin D)
  • Dactinomycin is used to treat some kinds of cancer that affect the testicles (testicular cancer), uterus, or womb (gestational trophoblastic neoplasia), kidneys (Wilms' tumor), bones and muscles (Ewing's sarcoma).


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 926

questions.stem: Which is not an alkylating agent:
questions.solutionHtml:
Fluorouracil (5-FU)

Fluorouracil (5-FU) is a cytotoxic chemotherapy medication used to treat cancer. By intravenous injection it is used for the treatment of colorectal cancer, oesophageal cancer, stomach cancer, pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, and cervical cancer.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 918

questions.stem: Topical MITOMYCIN-C Is Used In:
questions.solutionHtml:
Laryngotracheal Stenosis

Laryngotracheal Stenosis refers to abnormal narrowing of the central air passageways. This can occur at the level of the larynx, trachea, carina, or main bronchi. In a small number of patients narrowing may be present in more than one anatomical location.



Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 927
